title: Lacson questions P5B 'insertion' for 353 farm-to-market roads in 2027 budget
summary: Senator Panfilo Lacson on Friday questioned the House of Representatives' "insertion" of P5 billion for more than 350 farm-to-market road (FMR) projects that were not originally proposed by the…

blocks.text: Senator Panfilo Lacson on Friday questioned the House of Representatives' "insertion" of P5 billion for more than 350 farm-to-market road (FMR) projects that were not originally proposed by the Department of Agriculture (DA).

During the budget deliberations, Lacson pointed out that the 91 FMR projects originally requested by the DA were removed from the proposed 2027 budget. Instead, the House version included funding for 353 additional roads that had not been validated by the department.

"Kung ano iyong ni-recommend ki-nut, iyong wala sa recommendation, dinagdag. (The projects that were recommended were cut, and those not recommended were added). My question is, has the DA validated these farm-to-market projects against its farm-to-market network plan?" Lacson said.
Senator Francis Pangilinan, DA budget sponsor, said a review is ongoing for the 353 FMR projects.
Lacson said that around 30% of the 353 additional FMR projects were located in Batangas, Nueva Ecija and Iloilo. He specifically questioned why 19 projects were allocated to Lobo, Batangas.

Pangilinan explained that the proposed roads would support the area's livestock and coconut industries, as well as a food hub project in Batangas. He said the roads would serve as supporting infrastructure for the food hub.
Meanwhile, the senators also raised concerns over the funding for compensation of victims of the Marawi siege, nearly a decade after the war.
The Marawi Compensation Board is targeting to complete payments to all qualified beneficiaries by June 2028.
However, Senator JV Ejercito said the board still needs additional funds to fulfill its mandate, noting that around 15,000 victims have yet to receive compensation. —LDF, GMA News
